A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable throughout and describe the same authors' framework, OpenMMlo datasets, and matching experiments. V2 ends after its references and omits v1's appendices and checklist; these are observable document omissions, not extraction gaps.

before.justification: V1 reports original classification, OOD detection, image-text alignment, and ablation results in the main text and Appendix A.5.

after.justification: V2 reports revised classification and ablation results, alongside retained original OOD detection and image-text alignment results.

M1.justification: V2 introduces a sliding drift-adaptation window for model updates and a downstream mixture of experts whose T-router distributes features among FFNs (Figure 2 and Sections 2.2–2.3). V1 instead describes direct T-distributed embedding and classification without this expert-routing component. The spherical metric's change from tSP to Thp is principally renaming.

E1.justification: Reported classification coverage narrows from ImageNet-LT, iNaturalist 2018, and Places-LT to the first two datasets, although Places-LT remains in the OpenMMlo construction description. The four OOD datasets with tabulated results remain unchanged. Removing Places365 from Table 2's caption does not establish lost coverage: neither version tabulates its results, and both still mention it in the experimental setup.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds ViT, MAE, DeiT, LiVT, LPT, BALLAD, Decoder, VL-LTR, and LIFT comparisons while removing MEM. cRT and LWS already appeared in v1's backbone study and now enter the main comparison. Bl-Softmax/BALMS matches by citation and scores. Omitting Appendix Table 8 also removes MSP, ODIN, Mahalanobis, Energy, GODIN, and LogitNorm comparisons; Table 2's comparator membership is retained.

E3.justification: V1 Table 1 specifies ViT-Large; v2 evaluates its method with ViT-B/16 and separates training from scratch from a newly reported pretrained-CLIP fine-tuning regime following LIFT. These substantially change the classification comparison settings. The many/medium/few thresholds and CIFAR100-LT imbalance-100, ResNet-34 OOD setup remain unchanged. Missing training-budget documentation does not establish a budget change.

E4.justification: V1's Appendix A.5.1/Table 7 tests whether effectiveness persists across ResNeXt-50, ViT-Base, and ViT-Large; this backbone analysis is absent from v2. The pre-training/fine-tuning and concentration-parameter ablations retain their questions and tested configurations, although their scores change. The expanded main benchmark comparison does not supply a replacement backbone ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same means and standard deviations for alignment distances in Table 3. Neither specifies repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or a significance-testing procedure. V1's removed checklist contains only a generic statistical-significance assertion, not an additional documented statistical practice.

E6.justification: V1's Table 1 reports 65.6/82.6 accuracy on ImageNet-LT/iNaturalist with ViT-Large; v2 reports 69.6/81.5 from scratch and 77.6/82.1 with CLIP fine-tuning under different settings. These are replaced or new results, not established same-setting gains. Tables 4–5 also replace their accuracy entries, including the both-stage result changing from 63.8 to 69.6. Places-LT, backbone, additional OOD-comparator, and OOD-average entries disappear. Retained Table 2 per-dataset scores and Table 3 values are unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 adds a cumulative-loss optimization formulation over time-indexed models and a finite adaptation window in Equation 2. It removes v1's directional-statistics development and Appendix A.2's beta-distribution and normalization derivation. The principal spherical-density formulas and gradient argument remain substantially unchanged, but their supporting derivation is replaced by unresolved appendix and equation references.

C1.justification: The abstract and first contribution broaden the framing from long-tailed open-world bias toward unpredictable gradual and sudden streaming drift, with greater emphasis on adaptation from pre-training onwards. The principal claims about the unified framework, T-distributed adapter, image-text alignment, downstream recognition/OOD detection, and OpenMMlo remain.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly interprets long tails as gradual drift and OOD data as sudden drift. Section 3.1 replaces v1's scaling-law explanation for weaker few-shot performance with interpretations centered on successful pre-training and the remaining iNaturalist few-shot deficit against LIFT. V1's explicit vMF winner-take-all explanation also disappears. Most alignment and concentration-ablation interpretations are retained.

D1.justification: Removing Appendices A.3–A.4 and Table 6 eliminates architecture dimensions, input resolutions, optimizer settings, learning rates, budgets, batch sizes, hardware/runtime information, the FPR95 clarification, and explicit category-word masking instructions. This documents information loss, not proven changes to those procedures. The caption-generation prompt and code/data access statement remain, while the new window and routing components receive little implementation detail.

R1.justification: V2 removes Appendix A.1's substantial discussion of multimodal models, long-tailed open-world learning, concept drift, and hyperspherical modeling, including closely related T-vMF and T-distributed spherical representation work. It adds positioning through newer transformer and foundation-model classification comparisons, including LiVT, BALLAD, VL-LTR, and LIFT. Existing CLIP and decoupled-classifier citations are retained works, not new references.

P1.justification: The document loses its entire supplement and checklist, collapses the directional-statistics/adapter subsection structure, and rewrites the abstract, introduction opening, and classification narrative. The title and adapter terminology also change. This substantial restructuring leaves multiple unresolved 'Appendix ??' and 'Eq. ??' references, although much of the remaining main-text prose is preserved.

P2.justification: The workflow moves from Figure 3 to Figure 2 and is substantially redrawn with a streaming window and expert router. Table 1 gains backbone and training-regime groupings while losing Places-LT columns; Table 2 loses its average columns. Appendix Figure 4 and Tables 6–8 disappear. Tables 4–5 also shift away from their corresponding discussions, with Table 5 floating beside the conclusion.

improvement.justification: V2 improves the classification comparison by expanding relevant baselines and separating scratch training from CLIP fine-tuning. However, it removes derivations, implementation and data-preparation instructions, and backbone validation while introducing incompletely specified routing and window updates. Unresolved appendix/equation references expose these support gaps. V1 already contained conflicting hyperparameter reports, but v2 provides no resolved replacement. The resulting loss of reproducibility and verifiability substantially outweighs the expanded comparison.
